description: Return the whole /bots.json catalog of public agents and bots that pay, get paid, or connect a wallet. Output is { schema_version, generated_at, language, title, description, disclaimer, inclusion, schema, html_url, markdown_url, count, entries }. count equals entries.length. disclaimer is "Listed, not endorsed." The inclusion field states the rule: a public repository or demo, a known maker, a push in the 12 months before verification, and a license taken from a LICENSE file or marked unconfirmed. Each entries[] item is the same object get_bot returns: id, name, maker, description, protocols, url, license (string or null), license_verified, license_url (string or null), verified_at (YYYY-MM-DD), http_status (integer or null), archive_url (string or null), funds_or_keys, and notes. funds_or_keys is true when the software can access a wallet or keys. One unpaged response: no limit, no offset, and no text filter. Takes no parameters: call with an empty object. Use list_bots instead of get_bot when you need every entry, the count, the disclaimer, or the inclusion rule. Use get_bot instead when you already have one id and want that single object; an unknown id is an error on get_bot, not an empty list here. Use search_sources instead for papers and docs about agents. Use get_protocol_facts instead for how a payment protocol works. list_changes rows of kind bot prefix the id with bot:; strip that prefix before get_bot. A failed read returns isError. The text is the Error message (Fetch failed <status> <url> when the HTTP status is not OK), or Bot list failed. when the failure is not an Error. Free, no auth.
name: list_bots
title: List verified agents and bots
